categories.name: Uncomplicated recovery
categories.description: The case follows a standard course to discharge, with no recorded escalation of care and no extended observation beyond the ordinary stay pattern.
categories.rationale: The baseline disposition category against which the other four represent some departure — either in duration, care intensity, or discharge circumstance.

categories.name: Extended monitoring before discharge
categories.description: The case recovers without escalation of care, but the trace shows a materially longer observation period than the uncomplicated pattern before discharge.
categories.rationale: Separates duration from severity: a longer stay is not, on its own, evidence that care was escalated.

categories.name: Escalation of care during the stay
categories.description: The trace shows an increase in care intensity at some point after admission (e.g., a transfer to a higher level of care) followed by eventual discharge.
categories.rationale: Captures cases whose clinical course was non-monotonic — an escalation mid-stay — independent of which specific unit received the transfer.

categories.name: Early or irregular discharge
categories.description: The trace ends in a discharge that departs from the standard pattern captured by the other categories — e.g., an unusually short stay relative to the case's recorded severity indicators, suggesting discharge ahead of the typical course.
categories.rationale: A residual pattern distinct from non_home_disposition: the case still ends in a discharge event, just not one following the ordinary course.

categories.name: Non-home disposition
categories.description: The trace ends in a disposition other than a routine discharge — e.g., in-hospital death or transfer to another facility — rather than release to the patient's prior living situation.
categories.rationale: The most severe disposition category, kept separate because it reflects a different kind of case ending than any discharge-based category.
